html:
Roman general and politician who conquered Gaul, won a civil war and ruled as dictator until he was murdered in 44 BCE. His rise and death ended the Roman Republic.

He came from an old patrician family, and Marius was his uncle by marriage. In 60 BCE he joined Pompey and Crassus in the First Triumvirate, which won him the consulship of 59 BCE and a command in Gaul. In the Gallic Wars of 58 to 50 BCE he conquered all of Gaul and told the story himself in his Gallic War.

Ordered to give up his army, he crossed the Rubicon in 49 BCE and started a civil war. He beat Pompey at Pharsalus and in Egypt took up with Cleopatra. As dictator he reformed the calendar (the Julian calendar), settled veterans in colonies and gave out citizenship.

In 44 BCE he was named dictator for life. A month later senators stabbed him to death on the Ides of March (see assassination of Julius Caesar). His adopted heir Octavian became Augustus, and "Caesar" became a title for emperors.
